newsitem.title: CONGO: Zaire army chief killed by Mobutu guards - envoys.
newsitem.headline: Zaire army chief killed by Mobutu guards - envoys.

text.p: Zaire's army chief was killed by units of President Mobutu Sese Seko's elite guard late on Friday night, diplomatic sources in Kinshasa said early on Saturday.
General Mahele Lieko Bokungu, defence minister and chief of army staff, was killed at Camp Tshatshi in the Zairean capital, the barracks residence of the ailing president.
"Mahele was killed at the camp by the Special Presidential Division (DSP)," a senior Western diplomat told Reuters in neighbouring Congo by telephone.
The circumstances of Mahele's death were unclear but some sources said he went to the camp with units of Zaire's regular army to bring DSP elements under control.
Mobutu left Kinshasa on Friday and flew to his northern base in Gbadolite as Laurent Kabila's rebels closed in on the capital.
His government said the 66-year-old president, stricken by prostate cancer, had relinquished executive powers.
Shortly after Mahele's killing, armoured cars took up positions around Kinshasa's luxury Intercontinental Hotel where prominent members of Mobutu's 32-year administration were staying.
Since his appointment last December, the general had never been in full control of the DSP, a largely tribal presidential guard which at its height numbered 10,000 men.
Military forces from five Western nations -- the United States, Belgium, Britain, France and Portugal -- are in Congo ready to evacuate foreigners from Kinshasa if violence breaks out.
Several hours after Mahele's killing, there was no sign that the evacuation was about to begin.
